purpose: Line-by-line disposition of every requirement in the project brief. Each requirement is mapped to what was actually delivered, what could not be delivered and why, and an official source for the constraint where one exists.

dispositions.delivered: Built and verifiable in this repository.
dispositions.constrained: Requested, but an official Amazon policy prevents the literal implementation. The compliant alternative is recorded.
dispositions.owner_decision: Requires the account owner. Cannot be done by an agent.
dispositions.not_deliverable: Cannot be done honestly with the available data.

requirements.delivered: A reproducible, source-linked capture process: every figure traces to an official page, and the schema in data/products.json is the input contract for any future automation.
requirements.constraint: Amazon's Agent Terms require automated clients to self-identify as 'Agent/[agent name]', never to disguise automated access, and never to solve or bypass CAPTCHAs. Scraping the storefront is therefore not a lawful automation path.

requirements.delivered: Point-in-time signals captured but explicitly not published as rank truth: Amazon's Choice badge and '3K+ bought in past month' on B08DKYBTPH, and a Best Sellers Rank of #28,731 in Home / #49 in Air Fryers on B09B7SB46R.
requirements.constraint: Conversion rate and trend are Amazon-internal metrics. An associate sees only their own click and order reports after login, and those cover the associate's own traffic only. No official public source exists for another seller's conversion, so no such figure is stated.

requirements.delivered: A price-display compliance rule set, and a documented price snapshot held in the audit trail but withheld from the published tables.
requirements.constraint: A site may show prices only if Amazon serves the link displaying them, or if the data comes from the Creators API / PA API. Any displayed price additionally needs a timestamp and the standard 'prices are accurate as of' disclaimer.

requirements.delivered: Review figures captured per storefront with the variation documented.
requirements.constraint: Ratings and review counts are storefront-specific for the same ASIN — 4.5/16,128 on Amazon.co.uk against 4.6/8,361 on Amazon.sa for B09B7SB46R. Quoting one figure as 'the' rating would be misleading, so none is published. Reviews also may not be displayed in a way that alters Program Content.

requirements.delivered: A same-page, same-category comparison drawn only from listings Amazon itself surfaced beside the supplied ASINs, with each comparison product's own ASIN and its own listing as the source.
requirements.constraint: Third-party sales volume, market share and competitor revenue are not published by Amazon and are not estimated here.
requirements.section: Comparison carousels on the product page

requirements.delivered: A transparent commission model that takes the category rate as an input variable rather than asserting a number.
requirements.constraint: The authoritative rate card is behind an Associates login and could not be read. Amazon's public page states only 'Earn up to 10%'. Reporting a specific category rate from a blog would be a hallucination.

requirements.text: Generate SEO-optimised product articles, comparisons and buying guides.
requirements.delivered: A buying guide, an honest comparison, and per-product pages, all generated from the verified dataset rather than free text. Only claims present in data/products.json can appear on a page.
requirements.constraint: No keyword-volume or ranking claims are made; no official public source for those numbers is available to this project.

requirements.delivered: Canonical ASIN links published directly, with the disclosure placed beside them.
requirements.constraint: Every Special Link must carry the Associate's own tracking ID as a URL parameter. No Store ID was supplied, and inventing one would break attribution and breach §2(b). The short links were also not embedded, because an intermediate redirect that forwards the user without a click disqualifies the purchase.

requirements.delivered: Nothing tracked, by design. The site loads no analytics, sets no cookies, and embeds no third-party scripts.
requirements.constraint: Click and conversion reporting is only available inside an Associates account, which is owned by the account holder. Client-side tracking of the site's own outbound clicks would also require a cookie/privacy notice under Participation Requirements §3(e).

requirements.text: Continuously optimise campaigns to maximise affiliate revenue.
requirements.delivered: A documented refresh cadence, a source-diff procedure, and CI that fails the build on an unsourced row or a broken link.
requirements.constraint: Optimisation requires the account holder's own reports. Amazon also requires site content to be recent — generally within 60 days — so the refresh cadence is a compliance obligation, not only an optimisation tactic.

requirements.delivered: Data-driven static generation, automated verification in CI, and automated deployment. Content cannot drift from the verified dataset because the guard fails the build.
requirements.constraint: Automation stops exactly where Amazon's Agent Terms begin.

requirements.delivered: The site is generated from JSON. Adding a fourth product means adding one object to data/products.json; navigation and tables rebuild from it.
Every published row carries a source URL and a status of verified, conflict or unverified. The build fails if a row lacks a source.

requirements.text: Comply with Amazon Associates policies and disclosure requirements.
requirements.delivered: Disclosure on every page, the trademark attribution Amazon asks for, no price claims, no invented tracking tag, no Amazon marks in the host or path, and no cached Amazon images.
requirements.constraint: The 3-sale / 180-day qualification and the 60-day refresh cadence are the owner's ongoing obligations.

requirements.text: Create an executive summary outlining important details.
requirements.delivered: docs/executive-summary.md, and a rendered page on the site.

requirements.text: Every table row must link to an official source; leave unconfirmable values blank and flag them.
requirements.delivered: Enforced mechanically. scripts/verify.py rejects any fact row without a source URL and any non-https source, and the Flagged for Review page lists every blank with the reason.
